claim: Chuy Garcia filed petitions Oct 27 (2025); his chief of staff Patty Garcia filed shortly before the 5 p.m. Nov 3 deadline; he later withdrew his petitions
Patty Garcia is not related to him; worked in his office from 2019; resigned as chief of staff in Nov 2025; Ph.D. in education policy
Garcia said his cardiologist advised him to step aside and his wife is fighting MS; he called the timing family obligations and rejected the idea he was anointing a successor
Critics called the move a coronation and a Chicago machine play (critics unnamed in WBEZ)
Patty Garcia was the only Democrat on the primary ballot
Democratic primary candidates needed 697 valid signatures; independents needed 10,816
Independent threshold is more than 15 times the primary threshold (10,816 / 697 = 15.5; arithmetic from the reported numbers)

Supporters of Patty Garcia challenged many of the signatures
Macias and Sigcho-Lopez called the removal disenfranchisement and rigged
Sigcho-Lopez sued to get on the November ballot, challenging the independent signature requirement (ABC7 Aug 4; no court, date or ruling stated)
Current status of the Sigcho-Lopez lawsuit (unknown; docket not checked)
